exclude_why.squall/squall/parser/parse.py: Lark tree-walking parser with 33 standing violations (7 C901, 2 PLR0915, the rest no-is-not-none and one I001). Added rather than fixed when the change that first touched it was repairing a live defect: WHENEVER actions Db2 does not define were read as jumps, and NOT FOUND with one of them raised out of an enum lookup, which reached cobble's corpus parse as members it could no longer parse at all. cicada/cics/cics_parser.py is on this list for the same shape. Leaves this list with its violations fixed -- red-dragon-forge-3f3.
exclude_why._: Read by nobody: JSON has no comments, and an exclusion whose reason lives in another file is one nobody can judge later. Every key above appears here.

exclude_why.cicada/cics/cell.py: The one mutable slot CicsRegion keeps its position in. A pseudo-conversational region is a cursor over (transid, program, commarea) that advances each turn; the position itself is a frozen value replaced wholesale here, so the rest of dispatcher.py stays gated. It also holds the typed boundary to the one-element holder lists run_cics shares with the still-ungated builtins, which create them as [None] and read None as nothing held: the store (a list write, and a cast, since no invariant list type admits a [None] list later carrying a value) and the matching None-aware read. fill does the same for the region's program cache: it is handed to the CICS spec before the programs exist, since compiling them needs the spec, and every EXEC CICS LINK resolves against that one object, so it is filled in place, never replaced.

exclude_why.cobol_harness/: Ported as-is from tw-cc-codes; its primitives mutate bytearrays, program_cache dicts and queue objects in place by design (build_record writes into a bytearray seed, compile_link_targets fills a shared program_cache, VsamFixture mutates its datasets dict so the already-captured VsamEngine sees the additions). Refactoring the core primitives to a functional style would break the contract with cicada's mutable-cell wiring (build_cics_spec captures references, not snapshots). Leaves this list if/when the primitives are individually gated.
exclude_why.tests/: The rules target production style, while fixtures legitimately mutate -- `region[0:8] = data` on a bytearray reads better than any concatenation satisfying no-subscript-mutation. The suites also predate this gate, so touching one file for an unrelated reason surfaces its whole backlog and blocks the commit.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/asg_walk.py: The corpus's one ASG descent. It walks a document whose nesting outruns CPython's recursion limit, so the stack must be explicit -- no-list-append/no-list-pop/no-loop-mutation cannot all be met. Constraint comes from the ASG, not from style.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/cics/suppressed_transactio: The placeholder-transaction filter's one running counter, extracted from build_graph.py so the rest of that module stays gated. Its GraphWriter sink is push-based -- add_node/add_edge fire once per occurrence with no stream to fold a count over -- so SuppressedTransactions has to be state mutated in place and read back by the same object later. Mirrors cicada/cics/cell.py and cicada/cics/strategy_stores.py's justification: a rebuilt copy on every call would go unseen by the caller already holding the original reference.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/cics/exec_cics_walk.py: The walk that finds every EXEC CICS statement in a program's ASG for cobble-build. Linting it without this exclusion leaves only the walk's own loop: set.add, list.append and list.extend on its visited set, stack and results, the loop function's complexity and statement count, and no-optional-none on the predicate that sorts field values, because a field value can be None. The immutable version threaded a frozenset of visited ids through a fold and copied it at every object, quadratic in the ASG's size: 3.56 s against 0.018 s on CardDemo's largest program, with the same statements in the same order. It is typed without object: the stack holds dataclass instances and containers, under a recursive alias. Only the loop lives here, so verb_source_asg.py stays gated.
The combine's per-round memo: every vertex's join over all it reaches, solved by Tarjan's algorithm with an explicit stack, shared by every jump of the round. The memo, the stack and the per-vertex successor lists are updated in place; threading them through as values copies them per step, and answering each jump by its own walk is the path it replaced (480 vertex expansions against 60 on a 15-program XCTL ring, quadratic against linear in the ring's length, and a corpus round that would not finish). Only the loop lives here, so the rest of the combine stays gated.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/dataflow/srccfg/worklist.p: The reaching-definitions worklist. It updates one node's out mask and the pending set in place as the fixpoint converges; an immutable rebuild per step or full sweeps is the path it replaced (837s against under a second on the largest member measured, 9f3aad14), so no-subscript-mutation/no-loop-mutation/no-set-add cannot be met without that cost. Only the loop lives here, so the rest of dataflow.py stays gated.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/dataflow/fixpoint/rows.py: The JSONL boundary, and it exists so that `object` appears in one place instead of across the query surface. json.loads returns whatever the file held; a recursive `str | int | Sequence[Json] | ...` alias renames that ignorance without adding a check, satisfying no-object-type in word and not in spirit. Everything above the boundary works in str/int/tuple[str, ...].
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/dataflow/fixpoint/fixpoint: A deferred backlog, not a design constraint: the sweep in `_propagated` and the loop in `_swept` carry all nine, and `_eta`/`_propagated` trip C901 at 4 > 3. Pinning python-fp-lint to a concrete rev turned the previously inert ruleset on, so the file began failing without being touched and blocked a rename that changed one import line in it. Whether a worklist fixpoint earns the mutation the way asg_walk.py's explicit stack does is the open question. See forge-uar.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/dataflow/depgraph/: A deferred backlog, not a design constraint: the five files carry 145 of that package's 167 violations, all accumulator loops and nesting depth. `rev: main` in .pre-commit-config.yaml tracks a mutable ruleset, so they began failing without being touched, and pre-existing violations in a file blocked commits to it for unrelated reasons. See red-dragon-forge-bgk.
exclude_why.cobble/cobble/viz/render_cmd.py: HTML string assembly. The renderer builds Mermaid and vis.js payloads by accumulating lines and node/edge dicts; every alternative (nested list comprehensions over a recursive step tree, reduce over a mutable JS template) is less readable and no more correct. The rendering logic carries no domain logic and no state that outlives a single render call.
exclude_why.cicada/cics/tn3270/wire.py: The telnet byte stream. A socket delivers unframed bytes; turning them into telnet events and EOR-delimited records needs read buffers filled in place, and the accept loop runs until the process stops. Negotiation and session logic over these events stay gated.
exclude_why.squall/squall/exec_sql_scan.py: The EXEC SQL / END-EXEC cursor-advancing scan, now matched over parsed FixedLine code areas (squall.fixed_format) rather than raw source text -- the sequence-number handling this used to carry (a `(?:\d{6})?` regex prefix, and a second regex stripping leading digits from every parse_text line) is gone entirely, since a code area cannot contain sequence digits by construction. A functional recursive-unfold rewrite (in place of the accumulate-and-append while loop) passed every unit test but raised RecursionError at roughly 1000 EXEC SQL statements in one source file (verified: 900 passes, 1200 crashes) -- a real regression on a shared package, since the original loop had no such bound. This is a lexer over a cursor position by nature; the iterative loop here has no depth ceiling. Only the scan (Span, the span-finding loop, its match-to-span/line-offset helpers) lives here; classification and rewriting stay gated in preprocess.py.
exclude_why.squall/squall/strategy_stores.py: Builtin registration into the VM's process-global Builtins.TABLE, the one write the SQL lowering strategy makes to state it does not own: no-subscript-mutation on Builtins.TABLE[...] = builtin (the VM reads that same object back, so a rebuilt copy would go unseen), and no-object-type on register's builtin parameter (Builtins.TABLE's value type is the VM's own untyped builtin callable; squall does not own it). Mirrors cicada/cics/strategy_stores.py. Every lowering decision stays gated in strategy.py.
exclude_why.squall/squall/strategy.py: Six violations, all structurally forced, not deferred debt: (1) no-subscript-mutation on self._whenever[...] = ... -- WHENEVER is precompiler scoping, applied in textual order as lower() meets each directive, so the strategy's own condition -> action state changes as it lowers. (2)+(3) no-mutation-outside-init on self._scope in preprocess_program_dict and on a PROCEDURE DIVISION DECLARE CURSOR -- the RedDragonExtensionLoweringStrategy protocol hands one strategy each program's bridge JSON, then its statements, through separate calls, so the program being lowered can only be carried between those calls on the strategy; ProgramScope itself is frozen and replaced, never mutated. (4) no-list-dict-param-annotation on preprocess_program_dict's `data: dict` -- the protocol (vendor/red-dragon/interpreter/frontend_extension_lowering.py) declares that exact signature; squall does not own it. (5)+(6) no-object-type on handles()'s and lower()'s `stmt: object` -- the protocol declares `stmt: Any`; ANN401 (a blocking Ruff check) forbids Any in squall's own signatures, and object is the only type both narrower than Any and inline with the protocol's contravariance.
exclude_why.squall/squall/builtins/exec_sql.py: Six violations, the per-run session state of a Db2 connection: (1)+(2) no-optional-none on _ConnState.current and _current()'s return type -- a run genuinely starts disconnected, and None is DbConnector.connect()'s own return type for 'no such backend' (squall.connector, a protocol this file does not own), threaded through rather than re-wrapped in a private sentinel. (3) no-unfrozen-dataclass on _ConnState -- the one per-run mutable cell every EXEC SQL CONNECT/SET CONNECTION/DISCONNECT reassigns in place, mirroring cicada/cics/cell.py's Cell (a rebuild has no external reader to update). (4) no-set-add on ctx.open_cursors.add(name) in OPEN, (5) no-set-discard on ctx.open_cursors.discard(name) in CLOSE, (6) no-dict-clear on ctx.open_cursors.clear() at the end of a unit of work -- open_cursors is the per-run record of which cursors OPEN/FETCH/CLOSE/task-end act on, shared by every per-call context dataclasses.replace derives, so a rebuilt copy would go unseen by them. Nothing a lowering filled lives here: each call carries its statement, declaration and VARCHAR shapes.
exclude_why.squall/squall/backends/_stores.py: One violation, structurally forced: no-subscript-mutation on cursors[name] = value in set_cursor. SqliteBackend/Db2Backend each own one _cursors dict for their instance's lifetime; a later fetch/close call reads it back by name, so a rebuilt copy would go unseen -- the same shape strategy_stores.py exists for. It is a separate module, not a reuse of strategy_stores.py, because strategy_stores.py imports squall.parser.sql_model and .importlinter's parser-backends-independence contract forbids squall.backends from importing anything under squall.parser, even transitively (task-7 brief, forge-qhi).
exclude_why.squall/squall/binding_stores.py: Two violations, both structurally forced: no-subscript-mutation applying (offset, bytes) writes into the WS region bytearray in apply_writes (every SQLCODE/SQLERRM/host-var write squall.binding makes), and no-list-insert prepending red-dragon's vendor checkout to sys.path in bootstrap_vendor_path (the one process-global mutation binding.py needs at import time). Extracted out of squall.binding (task-8 review round 1: binding.py itself carries no fp.json entry and is fully linted) so that module's own code stays pure -- it computes writes/paths, this leaf module is the one place that applies them, the same shape strategy_stores.py and backends/_stores.py exist for.
exclude_why.catnip/catnip/catalog_stores.py: The in-place lookup table its holders write and read back as the same object, so a rebuilt copy would go unseen by whoever holds the original. Its users: jackal's DatasetCatalog maps a job's dataset names to backing files across steps (a step allocates a dataset and a later step, IDCAMS or job-end cleanup reads, deletes or drains it through the same catalog); catnip's SystemCatalog keeps its datasets, GDG bases, AIXs and paths between writes of catalog.json; jackal's AllocatedFileIOProvider keeps each open file's dataset, relabelled at its first OPEN OUTPUT; cicada's VsamEngine remembers, per CICS file, which record a READ last returned, and keeps each open browse, across EXEC CICS calls. Mirrors cicada/cics/cell.py and squall/squall/backends/_stores.py. Only has/get/put/take/values/drain live here; every decision about what to store stays gated in its users. The blueprint's Catalog/DatasetStore shells (2026-10-10 domain model, section 11) replace both.
exclude_why.catnip/catnip/system_catalog_removal.py: One call, a false positive of no-list-remove: SystemCatalog.remove(dsn) deletes a dataset's file and rewrites catalog.json, an imperative-shell operation on the persistent system catalog, not an in-place list mutation. The rule is the bare ast-grep pattern $LIST.remove($ITEM) and cannot see the receiver's type; python-fp-lint exempts only whole files. Isolated here so jackal/jackal/catalog.py and catnip/tests/unit/test_system_catalog.py, which make the call, stay fully gated (user decision, 2026-10-11). Mirrors catalog_stores.py.
